html:
SMTO-POL-0002 — This Task isn't allowed to use that tool

GUID: 130681c2-920b-4ad0-a6d9-17128bb18b14
Slug: capability-denied
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • The Capabilities chosen for this Task leave out the tool the Agent tried to use, so SMTO stopped that step before it ran. Giving the computer more access won't change this.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Capabilities next to the message box and find the tool named in the message. A tool set to Never, or not selected for this request, can't be used by the Task.
  2. If you want the Agent to use it, set it to Auto or Always, then send your request again. Your next request uses the updated Capabilities choice.
  3. If the message names a command-line program, such as curl, remove it from the excluded programs in Capabilities, or ask the Agent for another approach. Commands that call an excluded program are blocked even when the Shell itself is allowed.

What success looks like

  • The step runs, or the Agent finishes the Task with tools that are allowed.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't send the same request unchanged; it will be blocked the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Invocation preflight (native_safety.evaluate_invocation) found the capability outside the task's allowed capabilities under the selected or enforced capability policy, or the shell command invokes an excluded executable, so it was denied before execution.

What this means

  • The task's selected or enforced capability policy excludes the requested capability at invocation preflight. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The task's selected or enforced capability policy excludes the requested capability at invocation preflight.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the requested capability ID with the captured selection and enforced policy; distinguish policy exclusion from a missing installation.

How to fix it

  • Compare the capability ID named in the denial with the run's native_allowed_capabilities and native_capability_policy (enabled_skill_ids, excluded_shell_executables). Use an allowed capability, or deliberately change the capability selection and submit a new request.
  • Use an allowed capability or explicitly change the configured capability policy if that is your intent.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The requested capability belongs to the intended task scope and passes preflight under that policy.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
